text:
Maya: Short sync — we need to lock pilot GA gating criteria: SLAs, runbook owner, pricing bands, and monitoring by EOD. Pilot customers asked for concrete guarantees.
Jon: Proposal: separate SLOs for interactive vs batch. Interactive care about p95/p99 latency; batch cares about throughput/latency tail tolerance.
Priya: Draft SLOs: interactive p95 < 350ms, p99 < 650ms for seq_len <=1024. Batch: 99th throughput target = 450 req/s per dedicated node.
Arjun: For long context models (>1024) mark as "best-effort" in SLA table and document expected degradation. Can't guarantee p99 there without different infra.
Liam: Rollback rule idea: if p99 misses for 3 consecutive 10m windows OR total error rate > 2x baseline for 20m -> auto rollback to last-stable model version (or quantized fallback) on canary.
Priya: +1. Also require an automated PagerDuty alert + ops ticket creation.
Zoe: Support mapping: pilot customers get "pro" level by default. Enterprise customers get priority escalations and direct SRE contact funnel.
Maya: Who owns the runbook and paging?
Arjun: I'll own it for the pilot. Will create sections: detection -> impact -> run rollback -> mitigation -> postmortem. Will include command snippets and playbook links.
ops-bot: Runbook scaffold created: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/pilot-ga-scaffold — populate "Detection" and "Rollback" fields before cutover.
Jon: Docs ops note: add a short blurb in release notes: "Latency & cost vary by model and input length; see pilot SLA table." I'll add the devex snippet linking to docs.
Priya: I'll write customer-facing SLA language + FAQ with examples (tokens/seq_len, expected cost deltas). Will include explicit fallback behavior e.g., quantized fallback reduces cost ~25-35% but may change outputs.
Maya: Pricing — pilot: do we do tiered bands or flat trial rate? Finance prefers simple bands (dev/pro/enterprise). Need placeholder $/1k tokens or $/req for pilot.
Liam: Suggest pilot pricing: dev = free sandbox, pro = discounted usage-based (tbd by FinOps), enterprise = committed monthly + reserved capacity uplift. I'll draft numbers for FinOps tomorrow.
Zoe: Also clarify billing telemetry: reserved capacity charges must be separated from token usage charges in billing exports. Devex will show both in the console.
Jon: Monitoring checklist: p95/p99 latency by route, error rate, GPU util, KV cache hit ratio, batching efficiency, cold-start rate.
Priya: Add synthetic probes for top 8 customer prompt shapes and regular regression alerting.
Arjun: Ops detail: canary plan — ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% over 24h if no SLA triggers. If error budget burn hits threshold, immediate pause and rollback to safe variant.
Maya: GA acceptance criteria (proposed): runbook completed + reviewed, customer SLA blurbs written and in docs, monitoring dashboards & probes live, billing telemetry validated, pricing band draft shared with FinOps, support routing defined, and at least 2 internal burn-in days.
Liam: For pilot we also want customer consent for limited SLA (pilot-SLA) that contains seq_len caveat and best-effort clause for certain models.
Priya: I'll prepare the pilot-SLA doc and a short consent checkbox for customers.
Arjun: I'll fill runbook and include rollback commands, canary cutoff flags, and postmortem template. Will tag SRE reviewers.
Maya: Timeline: everything content/runbook + docs by EOD today. Pricing draft by COB tomorrow. Monitoring probes before pilot start. If green, 2-week pilot with 3 customers.
Jon: Small ops ask: ensure telemetry separates "reserved" vs "burst" usage so billing lines are clean.
Priya: FAQ will include expected cost delta examples and how fallback affects quality.
Zoe: Support readiness: define SLAs->oncall escalation mapping. Pro = standard oncall, Enterprise = priority path + SRE lead.
Maya: If no objections I'll lock these decisions and update the product launch checklist. :thumbsup:
Arjun: No objections — starting runbook now.
ops-bot: Reminder: file a #release-war-room ticket when runbook is uploaded.
Maya: Thanks all — I'll post links to runbook & docs when ready.
Jon: Thanks team.
